blocked.name: The Sweet Chestnut of Quinta do Castanheiro
blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, D.G. n.º 70, II Serie de 26/03/1945, girth 9.6m, age_register 800 (last measured 1989)
blocked.reason: Re-confirmed exclusion, not a new finding: this exact tree was already checked and excluded when Sintra first shipped (2026-07-28, recorded in archive/CURATION-2026-07.md and archive/LOG-2026-07.md). It stands at Quinta do Castanheiro on private land, and press coverage recorded it mutilated in February 2025 with declassification recommended. Hard rule on private land plus an unresolved vitality question after known mutilation. Does not come back without a source confirming both public access and that the tree survived the mutilation in recoverable condition.

blocked.name: The plane trees of Largo do Infante D. Henrique, Colares
blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, three entries tagged tipo=Arvore isolada, girths 4.12m/4.58m/1.88m, age_register 120/120/30, no classified decree recorded
blocked.reason: Not a single collectible point. Sintra Noticias (2022-03-20) and a local blog (riodasmacas.blogspot.com, 2021-03) both describe Colares' plane trees as one continuous roadside planting ("conjunto arboreo", officially 33 plataneiros classified together 2020-01-28) running "from the Varzea bridge to the Banzao on the road to the beach", fronting the Adega Regional de Colares. The three register entries near Largo do Infante D. Henrique / Restaurante D'A Varzea are administratively tagged isolated but sit at the same Varzea site the sources describe as part of the row; no source draws a clean boundary marking these three as a separate compact ensemble distinct from the avenue. Reads as the same non-collectible-point case as Barcelona's La Rambla planes (already blocked project-wide) rather than a walkable cluster addition. Also 4.2km from Sintra's existing 3.1km-span cluster (Colares is its own village; day-trip-only if it ever ships), which was the brief's own reason to deprioritize it below the castanheiro. Leave blocked unless a future pass finds a source that clearly separates these three as a standalone, named square distinct from the avenue.
blocked.also_note: Two other candidates from the brief's 35-unmined list were checked and found to be duplicates already published, not leads: the 0.8km sobreiro (Quercus suber, girth 4.75m/register vs 4.8m brief rounding, age 350) at 38.79621,-9.39565 is sin_002 (The Fern Cork Oak of Quinta do Relogio, 38.796,-9.396, ~38m away, matches on species/girth/age/classification decree D.R. n. 276 1996 exactly). The 1.5km platano (Platanus hybrida, girth 7.71m, age 200) at 38.79560,-9.38590 is sin_003 (The Plane Tree of Parque da Liberdade, 38.796,-9.386, ~45m away, matches on species/girth/age/decree D.G. n. 290 1951 exactly). data/research/sintra-register-candidates.json had already flagged both near_published matches before this pass started.

blocked.name: The Quinta do Senhor da Serra cluster (plane avenue, yew, two box hedges, mixed native stand)
blocked.species: Platanus hybrida Brot., Taxus baccata var. fastigiata, Buxus sempervirens L., plus a mixed native conjunto
blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, 5 entries at Quinta do Senhor da Serra / Paco de Belas, classified as Public Interest Arborescence by the Direcao-Geral das Florestas in 2001; ages 100-200, girths 2.1-4.35m where recorded (cluster_register.py groups them at 0.3km across)
blocked.reason: Private property, access by appointment only: jardinshistoricos.pt states plainly for this quinta 'Privada' / 'Entrada paga / Acesso por marcao' with a contact email and phone to arrange a visit (qsserra@gmail.com, 00351214310038). Confirmed independently: the estate is currently marketed as a residential property (savills.pt listing) and operates as a wedding/event venue (quintasparacasamentos.com, noivos.pt, zankyou.pt all list it as a casamentos venue). Fails the first of hard rule 10's three tests (can a visitor get in without asking anyone's permission): an appointment is explicitly required, which the rule names as a 'no' alongside a doorbell or a guard who checks. Also 12.3km from Sintra's town centre with no direct public-transport link found (Belas/Queluz area, a different orbit from the Sintra hill-town cluster the other 5 trees share); would need its own honest day-trip label even if access cleared, which it does not. A WebSearch AI summary claimed 'may be visited 10am-6pm (8pm summer)' with a viewpoint over Castelo dos Mouros and Pena Palace; the actual allaboutportugal.pt page was fetched directly and contains neither claim (no visiting hours, no viewpoint description at all, and a viewpoint over Sintra's castle/palace is geographically implausible from a site 12km away near Belas). Treated as a search-summary fabrication per the standing rule and discarded rather than used.

note_2026_08_22: Verify pass, 2026-08-22: re-checked the full 16-entry Sintra-concelho ICNF register (not just the passcheck brief's 20km-radius list, which mixes in unrelated Lisbon/Monsanto rows already handled by lisbon.json). Every entry is now accounted for: 2 published (sin_002, sin_003), 1 already-blocked private/mutilated tree, 1 already-blocked non-collectible ensemble (Colares), 2 newly-checked clusters now blocked for private/appointment-only access (9 register rows total), and 1 register coordinate error. The ICNF register genuinely has nothing left for Sintra within the day-trip boundary; this confirms rather than repeats the 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15 passes' conclusion. A brief general-web sweep for non-register candidates (Parque da Pena's wider arboretum, Quinta da Regaleira's sequoia) found only vague, unattributed mentions of species with no individual measurements, ages or precise pin, i.e. leads too thin to write up as candidates in the time available, not confirmed trees; a future pass with more time could try to name and date a specific specimen at either site.
note_2026_08_28:
Verify pass, 2026-08-28 (deepen pass off passcheck.py --brief sintra). Re-confirmed the 2026-08-22 finding rather than repeating it: of the brief's 34 unmined register candidates, the two flagged 'within 80m of a live tree' are confirmed duplicates of sin_002 and sin_003 (same conclusion as 2026-08-22, re-derived independently by distance calculation, ~32-45m apart, species/girth/age match), the 4.2km Colares triple-plane and everything past 8.6km (Monsanto, Restelo, Belas, Ajuda) are the already-blocked or Lisbon-owned entries this file and lisbon.json already carry, and nothing new sits in between. No new register candidate exists for Sintra. Spent the rest of the pass on the general-web lead the 2026-08-22 note left open (municipal 'Arvores Classificadas' listings) rather than re-running the exhausted register or Wikipedia-join technique (Portugal has no equivalent municipal-register Wikipedia article for Sintra). Two findings, neither delivered as a new tree:

1. sintraromantica.net/pt/visitar/arvores-classificadas (the Camara Municipal de Sintra's own classified-trees page, fetched directly, iso-8859-1, 200 OK) lists every municipally classified tree/ensemble in Sintra concelho. All of them are numbered, unnamed group entries under a site heading (Conjunto de Tilias frente ao Hotel Paris, 19 trees; an unheaded Volta do Duche-area group of platanos/celtis/freixo, ~18 trees; Conjunto de Tilias no Largo D. Manuel I, 19 trees; Conjunto Arboreo do Largo D. Fernando II, reported only as an averaged estimate across the group, not a single tree; Jardim do Rouxinol in Rio de Mouro, 11 numbered platanos plus 2 named-but-generic 'centenary' specimens). None is a single collectible point per the standing rule (same failure as the already-blocked Colares avenue): they are avenues and squares of many same-species trees with no single obvious place to stand at one tree, and the page gives no name distinguishing any individual specimen within a group. Not added to blocked as separate entries since they fail the identical, already-documented test as Colares; recorded here so a future pass does not re-fetch this page expecting different results. One single-specimen exception on the page, a wisteria ('Glicinias do Miradouro da Correnteza', trunk diameter 1.00m, no age given) at a named viewpoint: not pursued this pass, a liana rather than a tree and thin (one measurement, no age, no second source), left as a thin future lead rather than researched to a verdict.

2. The same municipal page's intro text names a specific, individually famous plane tree: 'Grande Maior', the literary nickname Sintra-resident writer Maria Gabriela Llansol gave a plátano at Volta do Duche in her book 'Parasceve', which the Camara Municipal de Sintra physically marked with a plaque at the tree ('esta arvore e universalmente conhecida e na Volta do Duche esta assinalada pela Camara Municipal de Sintra'); WebSearch results independently describe a 2009 municipal recognition of public interest for 'o platano da Volta do Duche' tied to the same Llansol connection. Checked whether this is a genuinely new tree before treating it as one: Nominatim geocodes Volta do Duche (OSM way 23688927, 38.7964784,-9.3866042) at 75m from sin_003's published coordinate (38.796,-9.386, The Plane Tree of Parque da Liberdade), well inside the project's own 80m near-duplicate threshold, and both are the same species (Platanus x acerifolia / hybrida), same general kind of claim (a giant, municipally designated plane tree at this one corner of central Sintra), with no source describing two separate giant planes in this small area. Concluded this is very likely the SAME tree as sin_003 under its literary nickname, not a second tree, so it is not delivered as a new candidate (would risk exactly the duplicate-entry pitfall this file exists to avoid) and not added to blocked (nothing wrong with it, it just is not a new tree). Recorded here instead as a lead for a future STORY pass on sin_003 rather than a verify pass: sin_003's story currently says nothing about Llansol, 'Parasceve', the 'Grande Maior' nickname or the municipal plaque, all of which are genuine, sourced, additive facts about the same already-published tree (sources: sintraromantica.net's classified-trees page for the plaque/attribution claim, and independent WebSearch results referencing a 2009 municipal public-interest recognition for the same tree, which a future pass should verify against a primary Boletim Municipal source before adding a specific date to the story, since the 1951 decree already in sin_003 and this 2009 reference may describe two different administrative acts about the one tree). No coordinate change recommended: sin_003's pin stays as is.
